label: Peplink MAX HD2 LTE
description: Mobile router with two LTE modems: 2x GE WAN, 4x GE LAN, 400 Mbps throughput, Wi-Fi.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink tech-spec sheet: Ethernet WAN port **2 (GE)**, Number of Ethernet LAN port **4 (GE)**, Router Throughput 400 Mbps, Wi-Fi AP Yes. **HD2 means two cellular modems** - modelled as wwan0 and wwan1, since bonding two carriers is the point of the chassis. This is the LTE SKU; the LTE-A SKU in this catalogue shares every port and the same 400 Mbps ceiling.

label: Peplink MAX HD2 Dual 4G LTE-A
description: Mobile router with two LTE-A modems: 2x GE WAN, 4x GE LAN, 400 Mbps throughput, Wi-Fi.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink tech-spec sheet: Ethernet WAN port **2 (GE)**, Number of Ethernet LAN port **4 (GE)**, Router Throughput 400 Mbps, Wi-Fi AP Yes. **HD2 means two cellular modems** - modelled as wwan0 and wwan1, since bonding two carriers is the point of the chassis. The **LTE-A** part is the modem generation, not the port count or the throughput - both are identical to the LTE SKU, so ordering by interface list alone cannot distinguish them.

label: Peplink MAX BR1 ENT
description: Enterprise-grade router with LTE failover: 1x GE WAN (convertible), 2x GE LAN, 300 Mbps throughput, no Wi-Fi.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink tech-spec sheet: Ethernet WAN port **1 / 0 (GE)**, Number of Ethernet LAN port **2 / 3 (GE)**, Router Throughput 300 Mbps, **Wi-Fi AP No**, PoE Input No. Two things here surprise people: the single WAN port can be reconfigured as a third LAN port, and **this 'enterprise' model has no Wi-Fi radio at all** - the LTE link is the wireless, and a plan that expects an AP out of it is wrong.

label: Peplink MAX BR1 Industrial M2M
description: Industrial M2M LTE router: 1x **fast Ethernet** WAN, 1x fast Ethernet LAN, 100 Mbps throughput, no Wi-Fi.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink tech-spec sheet: Ethernet WAN port **1 (FE)**, Number of Ethernet LAN port **1 (FE)**, Router Throughput **100 Mbps**, Wi-Fi AP No, PoE Input No. **FE means fast Ethernet** - 100M ports, not gigabit, and the router ceiling matches at 100 Mbps. In a catalogue where almost everything is GE, this is the model most likely to be dropped into a gigabit design by mistake.

label: Peplink MAX BR1 IP55 Outdoor
description: Outdoor IP55 LTE router: 1x GE WAN, 2x GE LAN, 100 Mbps throughput, Wi-Fi, PoE in.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink tech-spec sheet: Ethernet WAN port 1 (GE), Number of Ethernet LAN port 2 (GE), Router Throughput **100 Mbps**, Wi-Fi AP Yes, PoE Input Yes. **Gigabit ports, 100 Mbps router** - the copper speed suggests ten times the throughput the box can actually forward, which is the single most misleading pairing in this whole vendor's range.

label: Peplink MAX HD2 Mini
description: Mission-critical dual-modem router, compact: 1x GE WAN, 2x GE LAN, 300 Mbps throughput, no Wi-Fi, PoE in.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink tech-spec sheet: Ethernet WAN port 1 (GE), Number of Ethernet LAN port 2 (GE), Router Throughput 300 Mbps, **Wi-Fi AP No**, PoE Input Yes. Two modems and three copper ports with no radio: the Mini trades the HD2's Wi-Fi and port count for size, and a vehicle install that assumes Wi-Fi needs a separate AP.

label: Peplink MAX HD4 MBX (International)
description: Four-modem mobile router: 2-5x GE WAN, 5-8x GE LAN, 400 Mbps throughput, Wi-Fi.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink tech-spec sheet: Ethernet WAN port **2-5 (GE)**, Number of Ethernet LAN port **5-8 (GE)**, Router Throughput 400 Mbps, Wi-Fi AP Yes - the ranges are because **extra WAN ports require a WAN port licence**, which converts LAN ports into WAN ports. The base 2 WAN / 5 LAN configuration is modelled. Note this International HD4 MBX is **400 Mbps**, while the HD4 MBX 5G in this catalogue is 2.5 Gbps: same modem count and same chassis family, six times the throughput difference.
